pr_title: Prevent Stats Indexer reporting error if repo dir missing
pr_body:
Repositories missing their directory should not report an error from the stats
indexer.

Close #18847

Signed-off-by: Andrew Thornton <art27@cantab.net>
pr_comments: Could be backported to 1.16 - but should not hold up releases

issue_context.title: Error on dexer/stats/queue.go
issue_context.body:
### Gitea Version

1.15.11

### Git Version

2.7.4

### Operating System

ubuntu/xenial

### How are you running Gitea?

i run gitea by systemd /etc/systemd/system/gitea.service

```systemd
[Unit]
Description=Gitea (Git with a cup of tea)
After=syslog.target
After=network.target
After=mysqld.service

[Service]

LimitMEMLOCK=infinity
LimitNOFILE=65535
RestartSec=2s
Type=simple
User=git
Group=git
WorkingDirectory=/home/git/gitea
ExecStart=/home/git/gitea/gitea web
Restart=always
Environment=USER=git HOME=/home/git

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

### Database

MySQL

### Can you reproduce the bug on the Gitea demo site?

No

### Log Gist

_No response_

### Description

Hello
I see this error in the gitea log
What can I do to correct it?

```
2022/02/21 15:05:06 ...dexer/stats/queue.go:24:handle() [E] stats queue indexer.Index(409) failed: no such file or directory
```

### Screenshots

_No response_
comments: I suspect the repository with ID 409 does not exist on the filesystem

Yes - this is the problem:

The repository directory for repository ID 409 does not exist.

That is not a valid git repository.

A git repository is more than just a hooks directory.

how can I do to correctly delete this repository? because I do not see it in the interface of gitea
just rm repositoy and delete the row ? like:
```
rm -r ~/xxxxxxx/koha-env.git/ *
mysql -e "delete from repository WHERE where id = '409';"
``
It would be too simple :)

review_comments:
I think we are comparing against https://github.com/zeripath/gitea/blob/d3bf78ba3c67c5ed7beceb886a3f2540dc816c4e/modules/git/repo_base_nogogit.go#L50

That being said, comparing to error strings seems brittle. Can we instead export a concrete error to check against?
I think the error string is incorrect too, as I think the meaning is there is no repo directory at the given path. I think we should create a custom error for this and compare using `errors.Is`.
This error string is chosen to match the error string returned by go-git
Ok, in that case our hands are bound I guess.
